attrs.reason: Management attributes revenue growth to Columbia brand, prAna acquisition (~$56M incremental), Sorel brand, and a channel mix shift to direct-to-consumer. The evidence pack provides total revenue (E12), quarterly revenue (E25-E28), gross margin expansion (E37), and MD&A statements (E36, E37, E38) that quantify the prAna incremental ($56M) and note product category growth. However, brand-level (Columbia, Sorel) and channel-level (DTC vs wholesale) revenue breakdowns are not present as reported numbers (XBRL facts or MD&A figures). The only quantified driver is the prAna figure, which is itself a management claim. The other named drivers are not visible in the numbers, so the explanation rests largely on management's word.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 10.7% revenue growth ($225.6M) is accounted for by the prAna acquisition contributing approximately $56M of incremental sales in the first five months of 2015 (E36), strong Columbia and Sorel brand growth (E36), and a favorable channel mix shift toward higher-margin direct-to-consumer sales (E37, E38), which is corroborated by gross margin expansion from 45.5% to 46.1% (E37).

The May 2015 ERP implementation (E30) aligns with the timing of Q3/Q4 changes. The numbers corroborate the seasonal pattern and show no deterioration in collections.
